correctness.rationale: The primary endpoint counterexample is a compactly supported sum of pairwise-disjoint smooth bumps whose bad-ball families shrink to the accumulation point and force a harmonic divergence in the modified compactly Hölder \(p\)-sum. Translating this function to uniformly separated centers gives disjoint supports and exact \(W^{1,p}\) norm additivity. Thus \(T(c)=\sum_k c_k u(\cdot-z_k)\) is an isomorphic, in fact scalar-multiple isometric, embedding of \(\ell_p\) with closed range. For any nonzero coefficient, sufficiently small translated bad balls around the corresponding center miss every other support, so the source divergence survives after multiplication by that coefficient. Local finiteness of the separated translates gives continuity. This proves every nonzero vector in the closed range remains outside the endpoint modified class.
residual_risks: The construction uses translation invariance of the Euclidean Sobolev space and does not automatically extend to general metric-measure spaces.
The result proves spaceability via a specific copy of \(\ell_p\), not maximal spaceability.

Current Resultary and web searches found no prior theorem for this endpoint class.
